title: Cap passage sentences near 35 words
statement: Cap a passage sentence for young readers at about 35 words, and build complexity from subordinate clauses rather than from longer or rarer words.
example: Past roughly 30 words, a nine-year-old loses the subject before reaching the verb.
detail: The grade-3 authoring rules cap a single prose sentence at 35 words: past roughly 30 words a nine-year-old loses the subject before reaching the verb, so length stops being complexity and becomes an obstacle. Complexity is to come from subordinate clauses, not longer or rarer words. A grade 4 rewrite went from 470 words at FK 4.4 with vocabulary inflation to 793 words at FK 5.6 by removing the inflation and adding subordination instead.
against: A grade 5 design put its difficulty in the task and the text's structure rather than in its sentences: 'G5 complexity in this lesson is NOT long sentences. The FK 4.23 is deliberate — the text reads easy so the *task* can be hard.' (grade3-reading/artifacts/u4l2-build/g5-audit/G5-BAR.md, lines 77-78).
